did: Followed the Git Basics Sandbox on my real kestrel-simulator folder, in Windows Command Prompt. Created the repository, wrote the README and the project goals, set up a .gitignore and an env example so secrets stay out of git, and opened and merged my first pull request.
fixes: Added lessons on creating a working folder and a repository, and on creating the GitHub repository before pushing
Added a terminal picker: Mac/Linux/Git Bash, Command Prompt and PowerShell ('ls' isn't recognized in Command Prompt)
Explained the "dubious ownership" error and the safe.directory fix
Explained the "pathspec did not match any files" error
Said explicitly when to create the README
Rebuilt the commit lesson for when several files change
Added the "staging adds up" rule for separate git add commands
Started the sandbox on master and added the git branch -M main step
Added an "I am also doing this on my own project" switch to every step
Made the pull request and teammates lessons work on a real project
Added an "I use VS Code" switch with a terminal-to-button table
The tutorial went from 6 lessons and 42 steps to 7 lessons and 56 steps
learned: The sandbox was tidier than a real machine. It assumed a folder, files, a main branch, a GitHub repository and a Mac-style terminal were already there, and each of those assumptions failed on the real project.
title: Git Basics on a real project
